column1: # WHO IS CARRYING WHAT -- append-only. THE PACKED-LOAD MANIFEST.
# *** THIS FILE EXISTS BECAUSE THE PLAYER ASKED WHAT THE DATA STRUCTURE WAS AND
# *** THE ANSWER WAS "THERE ISN'T ONE."
# Day 102. Per-person kit was being kept in the `holder` column of
# inventory_log.tsv, which is FREE TEXT and holds one string per row -- so four
# days of careful bookkeeping had been written as:
#     holder = WORN: Dave, Torsat, Yrtone, Blartho
#     holder = ONE EACH: Dave, Torsat, Tristle, Frython, Hask, Ista -- 2 spare
#     holder = 15 FRYTHON, 15 Ista
# One row, one quantity, four people, and the distribution in prose. THIRTY-THREE
# distinct hand-typed holder strings were in use. `inventory.py --held-by Dave`
# is a substring match on that text: it returns "banded_mail 4" -- the whole four
# -- and cannot say Dave has one, and would miss him entirely had the string read
# "the four in the front rank".
# THE PER-PERSON TABLE THE DM PRESENTED WAS ASSEMBLED BY HAND FROM THOSE STRINGS
# and presented as though computed. That is the exact failure this repository
# exists to prevent.
# *** WHY A NEW FILE AND NOT A NEW COLUMN. ***
# The first attempt added `holder` to state()'s cell key. It works, and it
# FRAGMENTS THE OWNERSHIP HISTORY: historical holder strings are inconsistent, so
# keying on them split every asset's running total into disconnected pieces and
# `iron_spike` computed to -13 for one string and +13 for another. Reverted.
# L052 had already named both options, on day 95:
#   "Either inventory_log grows a notion of a packed load, OR THE OUTFITTING
#    STEP STARTS PRODUCING A MANIFEST."
# This is the manifest. And the split is the right one on its own merits, because
# OWNERSHIP AND CARRIAGE ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS: the party owns a kettle it is
# not carrying and carries Ista's own hand axe it does not own. Same reason
# light.tsv owns the oil, world_changes.tsv owns what is emplaced, and money.tsv
# owns the coin.
#   inventory_log.tsv  ->  WHAT THE PARTY OWNS, and roughly where
#   carry.tsv          ->  WHO IS CARRYING WHAT, per person, quantities summing
# *** THE VOCABULARY IS CLOSED AND tools/carry.py check ENFORCES IT. ***
#   who    a character name from campaign/characters.tsv, an id from
#          campaign/people.tsv or campaign/places.tsv, or the literal `party`
#          for shared field kit whose bearer is not tracked.
#   verb   anchor (sets outright) | move (adds, negative to remove)
#   asset  an id from campaign/assets.tsv
#   unit   as inventory_log spells it
# A free-typed holder is how this went wrong. There is no free text in `who`.
# *** EXTENDED DAY 103: THIS FILE IS NOW THE SINGLE "WHERE IS EVERYTHING" LOG.
# The player: "yes let's have carry.tsv become the single where is everything."
# Up to here `who` closed on characters + `party` because the file only had to
# say who in the field party was carrying what. inventory_log.tsv's `holder`
# column carried everything ELSE -- Wend's barn, Toller's shop, Wethersby, a
# named NPC -- as free text, THIRTY-THREE distinct hand-typed strings, and nine
# of the ten rows below are the migration off that text.
# `who` now resolves against THREE closed lists, not one: characters.tsv (a
# character, by name, e.g. `Dave`), people.tsv (an id, e.g. `toller`, `wend`,
# `dill` -- excluding kind=pc, whose people are already covered by
# characters.tsv under their Title-Case name), or places.tsv (an id, e.g.
# `wethersby`, `wend_barn`, `basecamp`). `tools/carry.py check` now demands
# LOCATED == OWNED, not merely located <= owned -- an owned thing with no row
# here is the exact shape of the headboard and the diary, which had an
# inventory_log row and no location anywhere for seventy days.
# `debt` assets (Fenn's 90 gp, Dill's 1.1 gp) are NOT here and never will be:
# they are money owed, not a physical thing with a location, and belong to
# inventory_log.tsv alone.
# inventory_log.tsv's `holder` column is retired as of this migration -- read
# ONLY, for the historical record of who a row's writer believed held a thing
# at the time. Going forward, WHERE something is lives here.
# *** WHAT `party` MEANS, PRECISELY. *** Shared kit that IS being carried, by
# somebody, and the party has never tracked which somebody -- the rope, the
# sacks, the rations, the torches. Its weight is real and must be apportioned
# across whoever is on the expedition before any movement rate is believed. It
# does NOT mean "somewhere among our possessions", which is what `spread` meant
# in inventory_log and which on day 101 turned out to include a lean-to
# twenty-two miles away.
# *** THIS FILE DOES NOT SAY WHAT IS OWNED. *** carry.py check reconciles it
# against inventory.py: nothing may be carried in greater quantity than the party
# owns, and anything carried that is owned by an individual (Ista's hand axe,
# Brand's) is flagged rather than silently counted as party property.
